```{r include=F}
df <- readr::read_rds("data/clean_data/cld_filtered.rds") |>

# Also read in the egg table.
egg_df = readr::read_csv("data/Branch Care/Data/structured_egg_table_20260130 Adam Walter.csv")
embryo_df = readr::read_csv("data/Branch Care/Data/MLData_Nov25 Adam Walter/Embryo.csv")

egg_df <- egg_df %>%
  mutate(
    ever_thaw = if_any(starts_with("thaw_day_"), ~ coalesce(. == TRUE, FALSE))
  )
```

```{r data_cleaning_inputs_and_functions}
##################################################################
# MASTER FERTILITY INSURANCE MODEL CODE - With Model Validation
##################################################################

############################################################
# 0. FINANCIAL INPUTS
############################################################

#Can adjust these based off of feedback from Spring
cost_per_cycle <- 12000
payout_amount <- 25000
risk_margin <- 0.20
admin_load <- 0.10
n_sim <- 5000

############################################################
# 1. TREATMENT COURSE DEFINITION
############################################################

df <- df %>%
  arrange(pat_id, treatment_start_date) %>%
  group_by(pat_id) %>%
  mutate(
    days_since_last = as.numeric(treatment_start_date - lag(treatment_start_date)),
    new_course = ifelse(is.na(days_since_last) | days_since_last > 365, 1, 0),
    treatment_course_id = cumsum(new_course)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()



############################################################
# 2. MODEL VALIDATION FUNCTION
############################################################
# To validate the models, we should review:
# TEST:
# - AUC: discrimination ability
#     >0.7 = acceptable
#     >0.8 = strong
# - Calibration: predicted ≈ observed
# - Dispersion:
#   dispersion = residual deviance / degrees of freedom
#   Overdispersion = variance > expected under binomial
# INTERPRETATION:
#   ~1.0 → OK (binomial fine)
#   1.0–1.5 → mild overdispersion
#   >1.5 = overdispersion → consider quasibinomial
#
# WHY IT MATTERS:
#   If ignored → standard errors underestimated → overconfidence
#
# WHAT TO DO:
#   If dispersion > 1.5 → switch to quasibinomial
#   If ~1 → revert to binomial

validate_model <- function(model, data, outcome_var) {

  pred <- predict(model, type = "response")

  # ROC / AUC
  roc_obj <- roc(data[[outcome_var]], pred)
  auc_val <- auc(roc_obj)

  # Calibration
  data$pred_bin <- cut(pred, breaks = 10)
  calib <- data %>%
    group_by(pred_bin) %>%
    summarise(
      predicted = mean(pred),
      observed = mean(.data[[outcome_var]]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Dispersion
  dispersion <- sum(residuals(model, type = "pearson")^2) / model$df.residual

  print(paste("AUC:", round(auc_val, 3)))
  print(paste("Dispersion:", round(dispersion, 3)))
  print("Calibration Table:")
  print(calib)

  return(list(auc = auc_val, dispersion = dispersion))
}



############################################################
# 3. MONTE CARLO SIMULATION FUNCTION
############################################################
# Simulates patient outcomes and cost distribution

run_simulation <- function(p_vec, cost, payout, n_sim) {

  sim_costs <- replicate(n_sim, {

    p <- sample(p_vec, 1)
    outcome <- rbinom(1, 1, p)

    payout_cost <- ifelse(outcome == 1, 0, payout)
    total_cost <- cost + payout_cost

    return(total_cost)
  })

  return(sim_costs)
}



############################################################
# 4. PRICING FUNCTION
############################################################

calc_pricing <- function(costs) {
  data.frame(
    expected_cost = mean(costs),
    var_95 = quantile(costs, 0.95), # tail risk
    premium = mean(costs) * (1 + risk_margin + admin_load)
  )
}
```

```{r clinical_pregnancy_model}
############################################################
#  MODEL 1: CLINICAL PREGNANCY (BETA-BINOMIAL)
############################################################
# NOTE:
# No AUC here because this is distribution-based (not single prediction)

clinical_patient <- df %>%
  group_by(pat_id) %>%
  summarise(
    successes = sum(pregnant),
    attempts = n(),
    age = first(age),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

bb_model <- tryCatch(
  expr = {
    vglm(
  cbind(successes, attempts - successes) ~ age,
  betabinomialff,
  data = clinical_patient
)
  }, 
error = function(e) return(NULL)
)

if(!is.null(bb_model)){
  
  print("Beta-binomial model worked!")
  
  # Extract mu + rho → alpha/beta
  mu <- fitted(bb_model)
  rho <- Coef(bb_model)["rho"]
  
  clinical_patient <- clinical_patient %>%
    mutate(
      alpha = mu * ((1 - rho) / rho),
      beta  = (1 - mu) * ((1 - rho) / rho)
    )
  
  # We should check:
  # - alpha, beta > 0
  # - alpha+beta magnitude (variance indicator)
  
  alpha_c <- mean(clinical_patient$alpha)
  beta_c  <- mean(clinical_patient$beta)
  
  clinical_p <- rbeta(n_sim, alpha_c, beta_c)
  
  clinical_costs <- run_simulation(
    clinical_p,
    cost_per_cycle,
    payout_amount,
    n_sim
  )
  
  clinical_results <- calc_pricing(clinical_costs)

} else {
  # Welp, the vglm model didn't work. Try using quasi-binomial.
  print("Beta-binomial model didn't work here - falling back to Quasibinomial model")
  
  quasi_binom_model <- tryCatch(
    expr = {
      glm(
        cbind(successes, attempts - successes) ~ age_group,
        family = quasibinomial,
        data = clinical_patient
      )
    },
    error = function(e) return(NULL)
  )
  
  if(is.null(quasi_binom_model)) cat("\nQuasibinomial model failed to resolve...")
  
  summary(quasi_binom_model)
  
  # Convert to dataframe.
  quasi_binom_model_summary = coef(summary(quasi_binom_model)) |> 
    as.data.frame()
  
  # Retrieve alpha and beta (shape parameters)
  if(!is.null(quasi_binom_model)){
    coef_qb <- coef(quasi_binom_model)
    
    print(coef_qb)
  } else {
    print("No coefficients can be extracted from binomial model due to above-noted model failure")
    coef_qb = NULL
  }
  
  sim_results <- patient_summary %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      simulated_p = rbeta(1, shape1 = 2, shape2 = 5), # example params
      success_sim = rbinom(1, size = attempts, prob = simulated_p)
    )
  
}

```

## Euploid Embryo (Binomial or Quasibinomial)

```{r}
############################################################
#  MODEL 2: EUPLOID EMBRYO (BINOMIAL → QUASIBINOMIAL IF NEEDED)
############################################################

egg_df = egg_df |> 
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = case_when(
    age < 35 ~ "<35",
    age >= 35 & age <= 37 ~ "35-37",
    age >= 38 & age <= 40 ~ "38-40",
    age >= 41 ~ "41+"
  )
)

euploid_summary = egg_df |>
  dplyr::mutate(success = pgd_clinresult %in% c("Euploid","Normal") & !is.na(pgd_clinresult)) |> 
  group_by(pat_id) |>
  summarise(
    successes = sum(success),
    number_of_eggs_attempted = n(),
    age = first(age),
    age_group = first(age_group),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

euploid_model <- glm(
  successes ~ age + number_of_eggs_attempted,
  family = binomial,
  data = euploid_summary
)

val <- validate_model(euploid_model, df, "euploid_success")

# Overdispersion rule:
if (val$dispersion > 1.5) {
  message("Switching to quasibinomial due to overdispersion")

  euploid_model <- glm(
    euploid_success ~ age + eggs_retrieved,
    family = quasibinomial,
    data = df
  )
}

df$euploid_p <- predict(euploid_model, type = "response")

euploid_costs <- run_simulation(
  df$euploid_p,
  cost_per_cycle,
  payout_amount,
  n_sim
)

euploid_results <- calc_pricing(euploid_costs)



############################################################
#  MODEL 3: SINGLE-CYCLE EGG MODEL (BINOMIAL)
############################################################

threshold_single <- 7

df <- df %>%
  mutate(egg_success = ifelse(eggs_retrieved >= threshold_single, 1, 0))

egg_model <- glm(
  egg_success ~ age + amh,
  family = binomial,
  data = df
)

validate_model(egg_model, df, "egg_success")

df$egg_p <- predict(egg_model, type = "response")

egg_costs <- run_simulation(
  df$egg_p,
  cost_per_cycle,
  payout_amount,
  n_sim
)

egg_results <- calc_pricing(egg_costs)



############################################################
#  MODEL 4: TWO-CYCLE EGG MODEL (BINOMIAL)
############################################################

threshold_two <- 15

patient_summary <- df %>%
  group_by(pat_id, treatment_course_id) %>%
  summarise(
    total_eggs = sum(eggs_retrieved),
    eggs_cycle1 = eggs_retrieved[1],
    age = first(age),
    amh = first(amh),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(success = ifelse(total_eggs >= threshold_two, 1, 0))

two_model <- glm(
  success ~ age + amh + eggs_cycle1,
  family = binomial,
  data = patient_summary
)

validate_model(two_model, patient_summary, "success")

patient_summary$two_p <- predict(two_model, type = "response")

two_costs <- run_simulation(
  patient_summary$two_p,
  2 * cost_per_cycle,
  payout_amount,
  n_sim
)

two_results <- calc_pricing(two_costs)



############################################################
# 9. FINAL OUTPUT
############################################################

final_results <- bind_rows(
  clinical_results %>% mutate(model = "Clinical Pregnancy"),
  euploid_results %>% mutate(model = "Euploid Embryo"),
  egg_results %>% mutate(model = "Single Cycle Egg"),
  two_results %>% mutate(model = "Two Cycle Egg")
)

print(final_results)

############################################################
# END
############################################################
```
